---

## Final Summary: All Rounds

### What Was Asked
> Which stable, non-toxic materials are efficient solar absorbers, and how can the lab find them with far fewer expensive calculations than brute force?
> Hit criteria: SLME ≥ 30%, ehull ≤ 0.05 eV/atom, no Pb/Cd/Hg/Tl/As.

---

### The Journey: Round by Round

| Round | Experiment | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** | Retrospective benchmark, full pool (n=1,362) | BO surrogate → 2.99× vs random; heuristic → 2.11× |
| **R2** | H1 pre-filter (gap[0.7–1.2] + Bi/Sb/Sn/Ge/Cu) | **Abort gate triggered** — recall 16.3% (threshold: 60%). Element constraint killed recall |
| **R3** | Recalibrated filter (gap[0.5–1.5] only) + 3-arm benchmark | Pipeline validated: surrogate 4.06× vs full-pool random; filter alone = 2.71× |
| **R4** | Live campaign: gap[0.5–1.5] → BO surrogate, ≤35 calcs | **13 hits in 20 calcs; 10th hit at calc #16; ~6.4× speedup** |
| **R4c** | Confirmation campaign (reproducibility check) | ❌ **Not executed** — session limit; result unconfirmed |

---

### What the Lab Learned

**1. The gap window matters more than element families.**
The H1 hypothesis (ns²-cation elements would dominate) was wrong. Widening the OptB88vdW gap window from [0.7–1.2] to [0.5–1.5] eV recovered recall from 16.3% → 61.2%. The element constraint was the dominant recall killer. **Lesson:** literature-derived band gap rules don't transfer directly to OptB88vdW — the functional's systematic shifts require empirical recalibration.

**2. The filter does most of the work; BO adds a significant but smaller fraction.**

| Component | Speedup contribution |
|---|---|
| Gap[0.5–1.5] filter alone | **2.71×** (~67% of total) |
| BO surrogate on enriched pool | **1.50× on top** (~33% of total) |
| **Combined pipeline** | **4.06× (benchmark), ~6.4× (live)** |

The filter is cheap and powerful. The surrogate is still worth it (~9 additional calcs saved vs just filtering and randomizing), but the filter is the primary lever.

**3. Heuristic screening collapses inside an enriched pool.**
The heuristic's gap-based signal is already fully captured by the gap filter. Once filtered, heuristic (34.5 calcs) barely beats sub-pool random (37.5 calcs) — a 1.09× advantage vs BO's 1.50×. Inside enriched pools, pure ML surrogates dominate rule-based heuristics.

**4. The real material families are Zintl pnictides and tellurides — not the predicted ns² chalcogenides.**
The 13 confirmed hits fall into chemical families not anticipated by H1:

| Family | Examples | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Alkali/alkaline-earth Zintl antimonides | CaMg₂Bi₂, Na₂AgSb, Rb₃Sb, NaCaSb, KMgBi, K₂AgBi | 6 |
| Chalcogenide ternaries / tellurides | NaInTe₂, MgTe, NaCuTe | 3 |
| Halide double perovskites | K₂NaInI₆ | 1 |
| Intermetallics / Zintl silicides/germanides | Ca₂Sn, Ca₂Ge | 2 |
| Rare-earth Zintl (supply-critical) | YbMg₂Sb₂ | 1 |

---

**Official count: 13 hits (12 excluding supply-critical elements).**

---

### Final Speedup Scoreboard

| Strategy | Calcs to 10 hits | Speedup vs full-pool random | Pool | Hit recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Random (full pool) | 106.8 ± 33.1 | 1.0× | 1,362 | 100% |
| Heuristic (full pool) | 47.6 ± 2.8 | 2.11× | 1,362 | 100% |
| BO surrogate (full pool) | 33.8 ± 1.8 | 2.99× | 1,362 | 100% |
| Gap[0.5,1.5] + BO (R3 benchmark) | 25.0 ± 4.8 | **4.06×** | 275 | **61.2%** |
| **Gap[0.5,1.5] + BO (R4 live)** | **~16** | **~6.4×** | **275 (unconfirmed)** | **61.2%** |

> **Critical condition on the live 6.4×:** This assumes the campaign ran on 275 candidates, not the full pool. The pool-size was not log-confirmed (confirmation campaign failed). The 65% live hit rate is physically consistent only with the filtered sub-pool; on the full pool it would require impossible leakage. **Treat as strongly indicative, not citable.**
> 
> **Critical condition on all pipeline numbers:** 38.8% of hits (50/129) in the full dataset are permanently inaccessible because the filter excludes them. The pipeline is faster per hit found, but it cannot find all hits.

---

### One Open Issue: Confirmation Campaign Not Run

The round-4 live result (13 hits, 10th at calc #16, ~6.4×) is internally consistent and passes all skeptic checks except one: the pool size was not independently verified. A second run will be possible once the session limit resets (~10:20 pm PT today). When it runs, it will be **reproducibility** verification (selection is deterministic), not an independent sample.

---

### Recommended Next Experiments

In priority order:

| Priority | Experiment | Purpose | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Rerun confirmation campaign** (session resets ~10:20 pm PT) | Log pool size; close the one open skeptic flag | ≤20 calcs |
| 2 | **Supply-risk second-stage screen** on future candidates | Flag elements with high supply criticality (Yb, In, Rb, Te) | 0 calcs (data lookup) |
| 3 | **H2: Heteroscedastic GP** (family-aware surrogate) | Reduce "other" family MAE from 7.33% → ≤3.8%; may improve live speedup | 0 calcs (retrospective) |
| 4 | **Broaden filter to capture the 38.8% blind spot** | Test gap[0.3–2.0] which has 81.4% recall at 3.5× enrichment | 0 calcs (retrospective analysis) |
| 5 | **Synthesis prioritization** of top 5 hits | Rank by: CaMg₂Bi₂, KMgBi, Rb₃Sb, NaCaSb, Na₂AgSb (all ehull=0, SLME>33%) | — |

The lab has answered the core scientific question: **a cheap gap pre-filter [0.5–1.5] eV combined with a BO surrogate can find 10 non-toxic stable solar absorbers in ~16–25 oracle calculations vs ~107 for random screening — a 4–6× speedup — at the cost of missing ~39% of hits.**
